key_insight: A quantum physics-informed neural network can solve nonlinear integro- and fractional PDEs by embedding the governing operators into a variational quantum model with provable approximation power.
engineering_relevance: This provides a quantum-ready framework for nonlocal physics problems that are difficult for standard PINNs, with potential use in scientific computing and simulation of complex materials and transport.
method: Affine feature map + variational quantum circuit produce trigonometric trial solutions
N-QPINN uses numerical quadrature for nonlocal integrals/fractional terms and automatic differentiation for local derivatives
A-QPINN reformulates the equation with auxiliary variables into a coupled multi-output PDE system, avoiding quadrature
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a quantitative $L^2(\mu)$ universal approximation theorem with $\mathcal{O}(n^{-1/2})$ convergence and numerical experiments showing improved accuracy over classical PINNs.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on quadrature accuracy, circuit depth, and the cost/noise of training quantum models on near-term hardware.
paper_title: Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Integro and Fractional PDEs
